content:
mira: Quick RFC follow-up: thinking about separating 'penalty-generator' (pure, deterministic) from 'weight-composer' (stateful, tenant-aware). Goal: let infra teams iterate on penalty logic without touching runtime.

devon: Sounds good. A couple of constraints: penalty-generator must not consult live health probes (keep determinism) and must be cheap.

mira: Agreed. Penalty input = (tenant_tier, region_hint, prefix_hash, candidate_meta). Candidate_meta limited to static fields (region, tier, model_tag).

sam: Caching: if generator is deterministic we can cache penalty_vector keyed by (tenant, prefix_hash, canonicalized_candidates). Need canonicalization rules.
kai: Tie-breakers: composer should include a stable seed per-tenant+policy-version so ordering ties are stable during canaries. Without that we saw flip-flop in experiments.

ops-bot: sim-summary: small-run (8k) -> decision CPU -3.8%, median selection latency -2.1%, extra wire +1.5% (penalty vectors). Job: sim-2026-03-22.

devon: Config surface: expose only 3 hooks in v1: region_penalty, latency_penalty, cost_penalty. Each returns [0..1]. Version the schema and validate sizes (max candidates 32).

sam: Metrics: penalty.gen.ms, composer.ms, penalty.cache.hits, deterministic_tiebreak.count.

mira: Action items: mira -> RFC draft with canonicalization; devon -> schema+validation; sam -> serializer + cache bench; kai -> canary plan and stable-seed generator. Target: staging canary in 2 sprints.
